title: From issue to reviewed PR
subtitle: GitHub Copilot in VS Code · Intermediate

scenes.title: Fix a bug. Verify every step.
scenes.body: One order validator. One small change. One peer-reviewed PR.
scenes.narration: In this walkthrough, we'll fix a small bug with Copilot in Visual Studio Code. Then a teammate will review the pull request using the GitHub command line.

actions.title: The defect
actions.result: True  ← zero should be rejected

actions.title: The outcome
actions.result: A tested change, ready for a teammate

scenes.title: Read the issue and set the target
scenes.body: The validator currently accepts an order with zero items.
scenes.narration: Start with issue seventeen. The validator accepts zero, even though an order needs at least one item. Keep the function signature. One and five should pass. Zero and negative one should fail.

actions.title: Open issue #17
actions.result: Bug: quantity = 0 currently returns True.

actions.title: Check the acceptance criteria
actions.code:
quantity       1      5      0     -1
expected    True   True  False  False
actions.result: Scope: keep is_valid_quantity(quantity: int) -> bool.

scenes.title: Scope the change in Plan
scenes.body: Give Copilot the issue and the relevant source and test files.
scenes.narration: In VS Code, select Plan. Give Copilot the issue, the validator, and its tests. Ask where the bug is and what regression test would expose it. Check the plan against the files before moving on.

actions.title: Select Plan and attach context
actions.result: Context from issue #17 has been added.

actions.title: Ask for a bounded plan
actions.code:
Find why zero is accepted.
Propose a regression test and the smallest fix.
actions.result: Plan: test zero, then change one comparison.

actions.title: Check what will change
actions.result: Confirmed: the equality allows zero.

scenes.title: Make the test fail first
scenes.body: Switch to Agent and ask it to add only the regression test.
scenes.narration: Switch to Agent and ask for just the regression test. Review the proposed test command and run it in the approved environment. The new test should fail because zero still returns true. That's the bug we're fixing.

actions.title: Switch to Agent and limit the edit
actions.code:
Add only a regression test for quantity zero.
Leave order_quantity.py intact.
actions.result: Agent proposes one test in tests/test_order_quantity.py.

actions.title: Inspect the new assertion
actions.result: Expected result for zero: False.

actions.title: Run the tests against the original code
actions.result:
test_rejects_zero ... FAIL
AssertionError: True is not false
Ran 4 tests. FAILED (failures=1)

scenes.title: Fix the condition and run it again
scenes.body: The comparison changes. The interface stays the same.
lines: Ask Agent for the one-line fix.
scenes.narration: Now ask Agent to change the comparison. Review the edit, then rerun the same tests. The zero case should pass this time. The tests for one, five, and negative one should still pass.

actions.title: Ask Agent to implement the scoped fix
actions.code:
Change >= 0 to > 0 in order_quantity.py.
Keep the function signature.
actions.result: One line changed.

actions.title: Run the same test suite again
actions.result:
test_rejects_zero ... ok
Ran 4 tests. OK

scenes.title: Review the diff before publishing
scenes.body: Match both files to the issue and the test evidence.
scenes.narration: Open Source Control. Read the diff yourself. There should be one changed comparison and one added test. Commit both files and publish the feature branch.

actions.title: Review the code diff
actions.result: The regression test is the only other change.

actions.title: Commit and publish the checked branch
actions.result: Origin branch published from VS Code.

scenes.title: Open the PR with evidence
scenes.body: Use the approved remote terminal once the branch is published.
scenes.narration: From the authorized terminal, open the pull request. Link issue seventeen and include the test result in the description. The example creates pull request forty two. Hand that number to the reviewer.

actions.title: Prepare pr-body.md
actions.code:
Closes #17

Reject zero quantities. Added a regression test.
Validation: all four unit tests passed.
actions.result: Feature branch already published.

actions.title: Create the pull request
actions.code:
gh pr create --base main \
  --title "Reject zero order quantities" \
  --body-file pr-body.md
actions.result: Created PR #42 · Reject zero order quantities

scenes.title: Review the PR from the terminal
scenes.body: A teammate uses their own authorized account and reviews the evidence.
lines: Read the PR and inspect its diff.
scenes.narration: Now you're the reviewer. Use gh pr view to read the description. Next, run gh pr diff. Check the one line fix and the test for zero. Use gh pr checks. Wait for required checks to finish, and confirm they pass. Once you've checked the diff and the evidence, use approve to record your decision. If the change needs work, request changes and tell the author what to fix.

actions.title: Read the PR as the reviewer
actions.result:
Reject zero order quantities  ·  OPEN
Closes #17 · Validation: four unit tests passed.

actions.title: Inspect the actual change
actions.result:
-    return quantity >= 0
+    return quantity > 0
+    self.assertFalse(is_valid_quantity(0))

actions.title: Check continuous integration
actions.result: Unit tests    pass

actions.title: Record a human approval when warranted
actions.code:
gh pr review 42 --approve \
  --body "Regression and checks verified."
actions.result: Review submitted by the peer reviewer.

actions.title: If further changes are needed
actions.code:
gh pr review 42 --request-changes \
  --body "Please verify the zero case in CI."
actions.result: Alternative when the PR needs a correction.

narrationBeats.text: Now you're the reviewer. Use gh pr view to read the description.
Next, run gh pr diff. Check the one line fix and the test for zero.
Use gh pr checks. Wait for required checks to finish, and confirm they pass.
Once you've checked the diff and the evidence, use approve to record your decision.
If the change needs work, request changes and tell the author what to fix.

scenes.title: Run the same workflow yourself
scenes.body: Try it on another issue in the training repository.
lines: Show the failing and passing test.
Ask a teammate to review via gh.
scenes.narration: Try the same workflow in the training repository. Show the failing test, the fix, and the passing test. Then ask a teammate to review the pull request with GitHub CLI.

actions.title: What you should be able to hand over
actions.code: Issue → Plan → Agent → Diff → PR → Peer review
actions.result: A pull request with evidence someone else can verify.
